analysis.title: Data Insights: Institutions Turn Bearish on Stocks; Fed Hike Focus Persists, European Risk Tone Improves
key_insights: Institutional sentiment on SPX and NDX (relative bullish vs bearish views, six-month rolling basis) fell to about -2z on renewed tech and AI concerns. Since 2021 there have been five comparable SPX episodes, all around notable market stress, each followed by an SPX rebound, strongest over the next 20 and 60 days.
SPX is broadly unchanged as of Nov 11 from its level when sentiment fell below -2z (Oct 22). The S&P 500 has declined about 2% since the previous note, led by tech (XLK about -8%).
Technical backdrop for SPX remains cautious. A break above the 50-day and 100-day moving averages, which are key resistance, would be evidence of an improving technical picture.

NDX sentiment is -1.8z as of Nov 6, above the -2z threshold but near year-to-date lows. Since 2022 there have been nine episodes below -2z, and levels near these lows were previously associated with reversals in NDX performance.

After Tuesday's stronger-than-expected CPI report, markets price a higher likelihood of a December Fed hike. Institutional mentions of Fed hikes have exceeded mentions of cuts since the start of the year and peaked in June (about 4z, one-year rolling basis), and remain elevated.

This contrasts with 2024 through late 2025, when cut-related discussion dominated. A sustained decline in hike mentions alongside renewed interest in cuts could signal a shift in investors' policy expectations.

Institutional mentions of French OATs have eased from multi-year highs while the 10-year OAT yield fell to about 4.7%, which may point to moderating market concerns despite ongoing domestic political and fiscal uncertainty.

Institutional mentions of iTraxx Main are back to average (one-year rolling basis) as the index tightened below 60bps. Spreads remain above levels seen earlier in the year but below those at the onset of geopolitical tensions.

sector_views.rationale: Renewed tech and AI concerns drove XLK down about 8% and pushed institutional sentiment on SPX and NDX to bearish extremes. The note describes this as a contrarian setup and does not issue a sector rating.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Tuesday's report raised market pricing of a December Fed hike and put inflation back in focus.
Institutional hike mentions remain elevated though off the June peak, consistent with a December hike.
Declining yield alongside easing institutional attention suggests French bond concerns may be stabilising.
Tightening to below 60bps, with institutional mentions back to average, indicates moderating credit concerns in Europe.

risk_factors: Technical resistance at the SPX 50-day and 100-day moving averages could cap a rebound.
Renewed tech and AI concerns could keep pressuring SPX and NDX.
A hotter inflation path could reinforce a December Fed hike.
French domestic political and fiscal uncertainty remains a risk for OATs.
vol_and_positioning: SPX institutional sentiment at about -2z (six-month rolling) since Oct 22. Five comparable episodes since 2021 were each followed by an SPX rebound, strongest over 20 and 60 days.
NDX institutional sentiment at -1.8z as of Nov 6, near year-to-date lows. Nine episodes since 2022 fell below -2z.

geopolitical: The note says iTraxx Main spreads are below those recorded at the onset of geopolitical tensions. It names no specific event or region.
